youtube.title: Bombardier Beetle: The Bug That Escapes a Toad's Stomach
youtube.description:
The bombardier beetle can get swallowed by a toad and still come back out alive. How does a tiny bug win that fight?

Inside its abdomen, the bombardier beetle keeps two chemicals apart. When it is attacked, they mix in a hard reaction chamber and blast out as a boiling, toxic spray, hundreds of pulses every second. In a 2018 experiment in Japan, toads swallowed these beetles whole. The beetles kept spraying inside, and 43 percent of them were thrown back up alive, after 12 to 107 minutes in the toad's stomach.

Subscribe to Stickstory for a true story like this every day. Which animal superpower should we cover next? Tell me in the comments!

scenes.text: This beetle escaped from inside a toad.
scenes.visual: Ground level in a summer field, giant grass blades: a big warty toad sits on the left; on 'escaped' its mouth opens, a wisp of steam rises, and a black-and-orange beetle crawls out over its lip and drops onto the ground in front of it.

scenes.text: The bombardier beetle's butt is a weapon.
scenes.visual: Close to the ground: the fez host kneels on the left with a big magnifying glass over a large bombardier beetle (black wing cases with two pale spots, orange head, long antennae) that walks in from the left; on 'bombardier' the label 'BOMBARDIER BEETLE' appears, on 'weapon' a red ring and arrow mark the tip of its abdomen and a red 'WEAPON' label pops.

scenes.text: Two chemicals mix in a chamber,
scenes.visual: A giant cut-away beetle fills the frame: a window in its back shows two tanks, one gold and one blue; on 'mix' gold and blue drops race down two tubes into a small chamber with a thick red wall near the tail, which starts to glow and throb; labels 'TWO CHEMICALS' and 'CHAMBER'.

scenes.text: and blast out boiling hot, hundreds of times a second.
scenes.visual: Close-up on the beetle's tail at ground level: an ant creeps up behind it; on 'blast' the beetle tips its rear and fires a thick, pulsing gold-and-red jet wrapped in white steam just above the grass, the ant is blown backwards and flips onto its back; heat shimmer above; red label 'BOILING HOT'.

scenes.text: Can it survive being eaten? Scientists fed them to toads.
scenes.visual: A glass terrarium in a lab: a toad sits on moss; a gloved hand lowers the beetle on long tweezers in front of its face; on 'toads' the toad's red tongue flicks out, the beetle is gone and the toad's throat bulges with the gulp.

Close-up of the toad with an x-ray window on its round belly: inside, the swallowed beetle keeps shooting puffs of gold steam; with every blast the toad's body jerks, its eyes squeeze shut and twitch marks flash around it.

In the terrarium the toad heaves and gags, then on 'thrown' throws the beetle out of its mouth in a high arc; the beetle tumbles, lands on its feet and walks away; a big red '43%' and the hand label 'ALIVE'.

Back in the lab, on the desk beside the terrarium: a big stopwatch on a stand counts from 0 up to a red '107 MIN' while a bloated toad hiccups; on 'minutes' the toad spits the beetle out, it tumbles through the air and lands on the desk.

scenes.text: Beetles that had used up their spray? Almost all stayed down.
scenes.visual: The toad's x-ray belly again, but calm: inside sits a beetle that has used up its spray; nothing fires, the toad sits content with half-closed eyes and a full round belly; labels 'NO SPRAY LEFT' and red 'STAYED DOWN' above it.

scenes.text: Their spray is a ticket out of a stomach.
scenes.visual: Sunset over the field: the toad sits slumped with spiral dizzy eyes and stars circling its head, while the little beetle marches off to the right across the ground; red label 'SPRAY WINS'.

scenes.text: Subscribe for a true story every day.
scenes.visual: A night meadow under the stars: the bombardier beetle walks up to the fez host, who waves; on 'story' the beetle lets off a small puff of steam and the host jumps, then grins and points at the viewer.
